tweets.text:
"When you ask Claude to create something, it's operating in a fresh context where it thinks: Oh my God, the user asked me to make an app. I'm going to invent the most brilliant visual style."

From @nateparrott at Anthropic on how to get Claude to avoid the same designs:

"It's going to be serif text, an off-white background, orange, and these bars on the edges of the cards. Because in Claude's mind, it's only ever done this once, so it thinks this is totally original.

So in our Claude Design prompt, we tell Claude, 'For this particular model, you tend to overly bias toward these two fonts and colors. So don't use them unless the user asks you to.' That tends to help a lot."

📌 Watch our full episode here: https://t.co/HPX5HjXafX

"Do you find being a designer more fun now that you can easily prototype everything?"

That's the question I asked @nateparrott (Anthropic). His answer:

"I'm a little weird in that I have an engineering background. Before Anthropic, I worked at The Browser Company, where we made a browser called Arc.

We spent a year in pre-production before we released Arc. It took us a couple weeks to build out each idea and see which worked.

Now at Anthropic, you can kind of do that in one to two days.

So you've really compressed the cycle of building. What you haven't compressed is the cycle of putting it in people's hands and understanding if they're going to use it."

📌 Watch our full episode here: https://t.co/HPX5HjXafX

此次攻击于北京时间 11 月 15 日上午 10:00 左右开始，涉及算力约 13 EH/s。OCEAN 矿池算力一度飙升至接近 50 EH/s。

矿场托管服务商 CoreX Hosting 最先发出警报。受影响运营商怀疑 Luxor 的 Commander 矿机管理软件可能是攻击入口，但目前尚未得到独立证实。

值得注意的是，攻击者最终未能成功挖出任何 BTC 区块，因此没有获得区块奖励。不过，矿工在攻击期间损失的正常挖矿收益无法追回。

目前攻击似乎已经结束，被劫持算力已从 13 EH/s 降至约 100 PH/s。

这次攻击没有偷走矿机，却直接劫持了矿工的生产力。

COINONE WARNS OF PHISHING AFTER SUPPORT VENDOR DATA BREACH

An attacker breached outsourced support vendor MetaM on Thursday, potentially exposing passwords, bank account numbers, national IDs, and wallet addresses from customer service records.

Coinone urged affected users to reset passwords and watch for impersonation scams, noting that core wallet and trading systems remain unaffected as it reports the breach to South Korean regulators.

GERMANY PASSES BILL LETTING CUSTOMS SEIZE CRYPTO OVER €100,000

Under the legislation approved by the Bundestag, customs authorities can hold $BTC and other assets of unclear origin worth more than €100,000 for 30 days before a criminal case is opened, with a finance court able to extend the hold by another 150 days.

Customs still needs factual signs of illegal origin rather than just a large balance, and permanent confiscation continues to require a fiscal court ruling.

The bill still needs approval from the Bundesrat, the chamber representing Germany's 16 states, before taking effect on January 1, 2027

tweets.text: aster, a crypto exchange, puts 99% of its daily platform fees into automated purchases of its aster token. it spreads the buying across each day and gives the bought tokens to veaster stakers. so demand for the token follows exchange activity, but the schedule does not absorb sudden selling. on november 15, aster fell 27.2% in 15 minutes, while btc fell only 0.17%. the data does not show who sold or how much the buyback bought during the fall.

luxor says just over a dozen accounts were hit in commander, its software that can change pool settings for thousands of bitcoin miners at once. the diverted hashpower earned real btc. a reported diversion address got about 0.08089 btc from an ocean block on november 15. luxor promised to pay miners as if they had mined normally, so the lost revenue falls on luxor. the total cost is not known, and no payments are confirmed yet.

a hyperliquid account with a long bet of about 1.38m hype reportedly added $8.3m usdc as collateral on november 15 and kept the position open. more collateral lets the account absorb larger losses before the exchange forces a sale. so forced selling from this account is less likely in the near term. across exchanges, hype open interest fell 10.8% in dollars from november 13 to 14, but only 0.5% in hype terms. so traders closed few positions, and the dollar drop came mostly from the lower value of the positions.

Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

And anti-Jensen board members know they’ll be held responsible for $1T in market cap erased if they hold out against the Jensen restoration. But these are NPCs, so they’ll buckle quickly.

Trump also realizes there’s no way that removing his top AI CEO, namely Jensen Huang, will somehow keep him on top in AI (sorry, SI). This “spy” nonsense is just like Russiagate, the exact kind of fake story that Trump himself was subject to, so he gets it.

After all, there’s really only a tiny minority of evil conspirators in media and politics who actually wanted Jensen Huang out of the company he built from scratch.
